requirements.text: The temporary-use spare tyre of the unit shall be type-approved in accordance with UN Regulations Nos. 30 or 54.

The temporary-use spare unit shall have a load capacity at least equal to one half of the highest maximum axle load of the vehicle; where its use is restricted to a specific axle, at least one half of the maximum load of that axle.
The design speed of the temporary-use spare unit shall be at least 120 km/h where the unit is a Type 1, Type 2 or Type 3 temporary-use spare unit.
The unit shall carry an 80 km/h maximum speed warning symbol, arranged in accordance with the specified diagram, permanently displayed on the outer face of the wheel in a prominent position.

Where the vehicle is intended to be sold in countries using imperial units, the unit shall additionally carry an identical warning symbol with "80" replaced by "50" and "km/h" by "mph", permanently displayed on the outer face of the wheel in a prominent position.
The warning symbol shall have upper case letters at least 5 mm high and the numbers "80" and "50" at least 20 mm high, with each character element at least 3 mm line thickness.
The warning symbol shall have lower case text with a line height of at least 5 mm, all text enclosed in a border and placed on a background of contrasting colour.

When mounted to the vehicle for temporary use, the outward facing surface of the wheel and/or tyre shall exhibit a distinctive colour or colour pattern clearly different from the colour of the standard units.
Where a wheel cover can be attached to the temporary-use spare unit, the distinctive colour or colour pattern shall not be obscured by that wheel cover.

The vehicle owner's manual shall contain a statement of the risk resulting from non-compliance with the restrictions on the use of the temporary-use spare unit, including, where applicable, that use is restricted to a specific axle.

The owner's manual shall contain an instruction to drive with caution and at no more than the permitted maximum speed of 80 km/h (50 mph) when the type 1, 2 or 3 temporary-use spare unit is fitted, and to reinstall a standard unit as soon as possible.
The owner's manual shall state that operation of the vehicle is not permitted with more than one temporary-use spare unit fitted at the same time.
The owner's manual shall give a clear indication of the inflation pressure specified by the vehicle manufacturer for the tyre of the temporary-use spare unit.
The braking and deviation test of the unit shall be conducted on a substantially level test track with a surface affording good adhesion.
The braking and deviation test shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.
The braking and deviation test shall be performed with the vehicle loaded to its maximum mass.
The axle loads resulting from the test loading condition shall be proportional to the maximum axle loads of the vehicle.
The tyres shall be inflated to the pressures recommended by the vehicle manufacturer for the vehicle type and loading condition during the test.

The braking and deviation test shall be carried out with the temporary-use spare unit fitted alternately in place of one front wheel and one rear wheel; where use is restricted to a specific axle, only with the unit fitted to that axle.
The braking test shall be carried out using the service braking system from an initial speed of 80 km/h with the engine disconnected.

For an M1 vehicle approved to Regulation No. 13 and fitted with the type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare unit, the stopping distance at 80 km/h using a maximum foot control force of 500 N shall not exceed 50.7 m.
For an M1 vehicle approved to Regulation No. 13 and fitted with the type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare unit, the mean fully developed deceleration at 80 km/h shall be not less than 5.8 m/s².

For an M1 vehicle approved to Regulation No. 13-H and fitted with the type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare unit, the stopping distance at 80 km/h using a maximum foot control force of 500 N + 0/−50 N shall not exceed 46.4 m.
For an M1 vehicle approved to Regulation No. 13-H and fitted with the type 1, 2, 3 or 5 temporary-use spare unit, the mean fully developed deceleration at 80 km/h shall be not less than 6.43 m/s².
The braking and deviation test shall be carried out for each fitting condition of the temporary-use spare unit specified in paragraph 2.1 of Annex 3.

With the temporary-use spare unit fitted, the prescribed braking performance shall be obtained without any wheel-locking, deviation of the vehicle from its intended course, abnormal vibration, abnormal tyre wear during the test or excessive steering correction.
